source_authority.document: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
loci: Chapter 6 treats finite two-player one-round entangled games with a normalized question distribution, a Boolean winning predicate, finite nonempty answer alphabets, and entangled value defined as the supremum over finite-dimensional tensor-product strategies.

Theorem 1.1 states that there is a universal constant c_qs>0 such that, when the soundness gap epsilon=1-omega*(G) is positive, omega*(G^n) is at most exp(-c_qs * epsilon^13/(epsilon+log(|A||B|)) * n) for every integer n>=1.
The source convention ranges over arbitrary finite local Hilbert-space dimensions and uses a supremum; it does not impose a common Alice/Bob dimension and does not require the optimum to be attained.

definition_concordance.game_model: Lean Game carries finite question and answer types, a nonnegative questionWeight normalized to total mass 1, and a Boolean predicate, matching the finite one-round source game data.
definition_concordance.parallel_repetition: Game.repeat uses product question weights and requires the predicate to hold in every coordinate, so repeatedEntangledValue G n is the entangled value of the n-fold product game G^n.
definition_concordance.strategy_model: Lean Strategy has independent finite Alice and Bob carrier types, a positive trace-one density matrix on Alice x Bob, and question-indexed POVMs for each player. The carriers are not required to have a common dimension. Relative to the source's arbitrary finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, this is the standard finite-coordinate presentation after choosing orthonormal bases; no dimension bound is introduced.
definition_concordance.entangled_value: entangledValue is sSup of the range of Strategy.winProbability over all Lean strategies. Thus the target uses a supremum rather than a maximum and introduces no optimizer-attainment assumption. The coordinate presentation is semantically equivalent on finite-dimensional source strategies, but this audit does not claim literal definitional identity with an abstract Hilbert-space formulation.
definition_concordance.gap_exponent_denominator: distributionUniformExponential sets epsilon exactly to 1-entangledValue G, requires it positive, requires Nonempty A and Nonempty B, uses exponent 13, denominator epsilon + Real.log(card A * card B), and quantifies over n with 0<n.
definition_concordance.qualitative_consequence: StandardQuantumParallelRepetition G is entangledValue G < 1 -> HasExponentialBound (repeatedEntangledValue G). On nonempty answer alphabets it is a direct qualitative consequence of the quantitative theorem. The target itself omits answer-nonemptiness and therefore additionally covers formal empty-answer edge cases outside the manuscript's declared game domain.

target_audits.source_relation: This is the Chapter 6 Theorem 1.1 bound with epsilon=1-omega*(G), the same universal positive constant form, epsilon^13, epsilon+log(|A||B|), nonempty answer alphabets, and every n>=1.
target_audits.formal_relation: The comparator target states the same inequality with entangledValue, repeatedEntangledValue, Real.log, Fintype.card, explicit Nonempty A/B, 0<1-entangledValue G, and 0<n. The solution routes the target through pdf_distributionUniformExponential_unconditional / pdf_distributionUniformExponential_of_uniform_source_rounding and unconditionalSourceOneGameRounding_uniform.

target_audits.source_relation: For source-domain games with nonempty answer alphabets, Theorem 1.1 immediately implies game-dependent exponential decay whenever omega*(G)<1.
target_audits.formal_relation: The target states exactly entangledValue G < 1 -> HasExponentialBound (repeatedEntangledValue G). Its solution passes through exact_standardQuantumParallelRepetition_of_source_rounding and exactSourceOneGameRounding_unconditional. Because the target does not require Nonempty A/B, it is formally stronger only on empty-answer edge cases that the source theorem does not claim.

evidence: Nonempty A and Nonempty B are explicit hypotheses of the quantitative target, so Fintype.card A and Fintype.card B are positive and the logarithmic alphabet term is well-defined in the intended source regime.
The quantitative target explicitly assumes 0 < 1-entangledValue G and 0 < n, so neither the soundness-gap nor repetition-count quantifier is discharged by a zero boundary case.
The Lean game distribution is normalized to total mass 1; hence a constructed Game cannot hide an empty question-distribution domain behind an unnormalized zero measure.

The solution includes pdfAlphabetEntropy_nonneg from answer nonemptiness and exactSourceAnswerTypes_nonempty_of_remaining in the source-rounding path, providing explicit nonemptiness handling rather than silently taking log 0.
The qualitative target's additional empty-answer cases are identified as a formal extension and are not attributed to the manuscript.

proof_path_evidence: The uniform quantitative path is supplied by unconditionalSourceOneGameRounding_uniform.
exactSourceOneGameRounding_unconditional constructs the exact one-game rounding object used for the qualitative theorem.
standardQuantumParallelRepetition is routed through exact_standardQuantumParallelRepetition_of_source_rounding G (exactSourceOneGameRounding_unconditional G).

The solution separately proves probability normalization and bounds, including outcomeProbability_normalized, winProbability_le_one, winProbabilities_bddAbove, entangledValue_le_one, and entangledValue_nonneg.

disposition.basis: The quantitative target matches Chapter 6 Theorem 1.1 at the declared finite-dimensional tensor-product boundary: normalized game data, arbitrary independent finite local dimensions in coordinate form, density matrix and POVMs, supremum entangled value, nonempty answers, exact soundness gap, exponent 13, logarithmic alphabet denominator, and n>=1 all align. The qualitative target is source-faithful on that manuscript domain but is explicitly classified as a formal extension on empty-answer edge cases because its statement omits Nonempty A/B.

claim_boundary: This candidate is limited to current-root semantic/nonvacuity classification of the two registered OTP-G-QUANTUM-PARALLEL-REPETITION targets. It treats Lean's independent finite Alice/Bob carrier types and matrix-valued density/POVM data as a finite-coordinate presentation of the manuscript's arbitrary finite-dimensional tensor-product strategy convention; it does not claim literal definitional identity with an abstract Hilbert-space presentation. It records that entangledValue is an sSup and therefore introduces neither a fixed-dimension cutoff nor an optimizer-attainment assumption. distributionUniformExponential is classified as a source-faithful exact coordinate projection of Chapter 6 Theorem 1.1. standardQuantumParallelRepetition is source-faithful on the manuscript's nonempty-answer domain but formally extends to empty-answer edge cases, and that extension is not attributed to the manuscript. It creates no MATHSOLVE handoff, MATHCERT route/output, independent proof certification, mathematical-proof promotion, whole-chapter equivalence, or aggregate OpenAI Ten Proofs authority.
